Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the GridPower Holdings Q3 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to GridPower Holdings' Q3 Earnings Call. Joining me on the call today are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Maria Gonzalez, Chief Financial Officer; David Chen, Chief Operating Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Strategy Officer; Robert Kim, Chief Technology Officer; and Emily Torres, Chief Regulatory Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that statements made during this call that are not historical facts are forward-looking statements and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied. Please refer to our SEC filings for a detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Johnathan Hale.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on our performance this quarter. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities, delivering solid results in a challenging environment.

Our performance was driven by seven key areas: first, narrowing the gap between our authorized and earned return on equity; second, strong customer growth and usage trends across residential, commercial, and industrial segments; third, our effective storm response and recovery efforts; fourth, significant investments in renewable energy and the clean energy transition; fifth, improved reliability metrics including SAIDI and SAIFI along with overall system performance; sixth, robust rate base growth and the factors influencing it; and seventh, the strategic retirement of fossil fuel plants coupled with our replacement strategies.

Let me provide some more detail on these areas starting with our authorized versus earned return on equity analysis, which is critical to our regulated operations. Authorized ROE is the return approved by regulators like FERC for transmission and state PUCs in Texas, the Midwest, and Southeast for inclusion in rates, calculated on average net rate base covering generation, transmission, and distribution. Our weighted average authorized ROE is 9.75% from recent settlements, based on DCF cost of equity, CAPM with betas of 0.85 to 0.95, and risk premiums reflecting our mix of natural gas combined-cycle, nuclear uprates, and renewables. Earned ROE is our actual return, net income over average common equity, and the gap highlights recovery effectiveness and cost dynamics. Utilities aim to stay within 50 basis points of authorized to dodge scrutiny from deadbands or true-ups, as in FERC's recent Brattle Group study.

Over five years, earned ROE averaged 8.62%, trailing by 113 basis points, similar to peers amid supply disruptions and fuel swings. Breaking it down: in 2020, authorized 9.80%, earned 8.45%, gap negative 135 due to COVID O&M deferrals; 2021, 9.75% authorized, 8.72% earned, minus 103 from Winter Storm Uri; 2022, 9.70% and 8.91%, minus 79 on supply chain delays; 2023, 9.75% and 8.68%, minus 107 from nat gas hedge losses; and Q3 2024 year-to-date, authorized 9.75%, earned a stronger 8.94%, gap narrowed to minus 81 basis points—our best in three years, beating the industry median of 95 per S&P Global. This came from $2.1 billion equity rate base growth, including $1.4 billion CWIP for 1.2 GW solar-plus-storage in ERCOT and MISO South, with AFUDC adding 22 basis points versus 18 last year via formula rates in Texas and Missouri pilots.

Regionally, ERCOT at 45% of rate base has authorized 10.25%, earned 9.87%, gap 38 basis points, boosted by 200 MW Falcon battery dispatch in summer peaks offsetting heatwaves, though Uri costs linger. MISO, 30% of rate base, authorized 9.50%, earned 8.42%, gap 108, hit by 12% wind curtailments on 800 MW Illinois fleet but aided by $600 million in 345 kV reconductoring under MISO LRTP and MYRP filings targeting 9.2%. Southeast SPP/SERC, 25%, authorized 9.40%, earned 8.76%, gap 64, supported by Callaway nuclear uprates to plus 1.3% capacity and gas conversions with Henry Hub at $2.85 per MMBtu, despite SPP heat rates at 7,200 Btu/kWh. FERC's proposed rulemaking PL21-5 may pressure proxies to 9.2-9.5%, but our 15% merchant gas hedges it.

The 81 basis point gap breaks into revenue recovery lag at 45%, or $175 million under-recovered O&M from 2023 storms offset by Texas decoupling and quarterly true-ups on 70% transmission revenues; capex timing at 30%, with $1.8 billion YTD in IRA-eligible assets like 500 MW bifacial solar, 65% rolled into rates but CWIP adding $120 million pretax; and fuel/market at 25%, with nat gas hedges at $3.20 per MMBtu but $45 million coal-to-gas decommissioning, offset by 18 basis points from PTC/ITC pass-throughs. We're pursuing five pillars: $2.5 billion in DERMS and synchrophasors for Order 881, 25 basis points uplift by 2026; 3 GW renewables like Orsted offshore pilots with IRA 30% ITC plus 10% domestic bonus to hit 45% carbon-free by 2027 per EPA COLR; AI predictive maintenance on Siemens SGT6-8000H cutting outages 22%, saving $80 million O&M; rate cases in MISO for 10.0% ROE citing wildfire risks; and $1.2 billion green bonds at 4.85% for 12-15% rate base growth. For FY2024, earned ROE guides to 9.05-9.25%, gap 50-70 basis points, converging to 25 by 2025-2027 with $7 billion capex at 8% CAGR and 6-8% EPS growth, resilient versus merchant peers.

Next, customer growth and usage trends. We added 45,000 net new customers year-over-year, 1.8% growth to 2.55 million across eight states from Northeast to Southeast and Midwest, with 2.1% weather-normalized load growth to 28.4 million MWh sales, up 3.2%. Residential, 42% of revenue, grew 2.5% or 32,000 accounts in Sun Belt like Florida and Texas on migration and 4.1% housing starts; usage per customer up 1.8% to 1,120 kWh/month from EV surge 28% to 150,000 vehicles adding 50 MW evening loads, 15% heat pumps via $50 million rebates boosting winter kWh 2-3%, and 12% above-normal cooling days hitting 14.2 GW peak—we're deploying 500 MW grid-edge batteries with Fluence and Tesla for 15% duck curve reduction by 2025, guiding 2.5-3.0% growth versus EIA's 1.2%. Commercial, 28% of sales, 1.2% or 8,500 adds slowed by hybrid work but usage up 2.4% to 45 MWh/customer on data centers like AWS and Google 100+ MW campuses at PUE below 1.2, plus Southeast tourism; DLR sensors on 1,200 miles unlock 10-15% capacity, with 15-year PPAs for 500 MW solar-storage at 90% renewables for RPS—expect 2.0-2.5%, half from data centers. Industrial, 30%, 0.8% or 4,500 adds but 4.6% usage to 2.8 million MWh on reshoring like TSMC fabs at 200 MW and steel EAFs at 400-500 kWh/ton to 72% load factor; Texas LNG/crypto up 7% with $12 million demand response; $200 million in PMUs/DERMS for 1.2 GW rooftop solar, plus 1 GW industrial renewables with Siemens hydrogen—3.5-4.0% growth on CHIPS Act. Overall, 2.5% customer and 2.8-3.2% load growth FY24 with $1.2 billion grid hardening and 500 EV chargers, supporting 6-8% EPS at A- credit.

Turning to storm response and recovery after Hurricane Zeta, a Category 3 landfall October 15th in Gulf Coast with 120 mph winds and 12-foot surges in Baton Rouge and Mobile. Peak outages hit 1.47 million customers or 28% base, akin to Ida's 1.6 million but below Ian's 2.1 million. OMS with SCADA triaged, GIS dispatch hit 85% critical infrastructure in four hours. ICS with NERC/EEI mobilized 12,000 workers including 4,500 from 22 states like Duke, Entergy, Southern; drones surveyed 2,500 miles identifying 15,000 poles, 20% efficiency gain; FLIR trucks cut cable digs 35%. Restored 90% in 72 hours ahead of 96-hour target, full by day 7 except 2,500 remote; SAIDI 145 minutes, 15% better than Ida via $450 million grid modernization and 250,000 Louisiana AMI for feeder reconfiguration. Opex $285 million Q3, $175 million Zeta up 12% on materials/labor; capex $420 million YTD including $110 million hardening like 120 miles undergrounding and 500 AI reclosers from GE Vernova cutting SAIFI 22%. Insurance $210 million probable net of deductibles, $85 million advances; FPLA/LPSC approvals for riders/securitization ensure no dilution. NOAA notes 25% hurricane uptick; Everglades minimal via 40,000 miles ROW trim reducing tree outages 40%, Louisiana 55% poles. $2.5 billion resiliency plan: Weather AI with IBM improving predictions 18% islanding 50 MW microgrids; FRP poles 30% fleet, Xcel-style BESS trailers; IBEW training 800 linemen, dual-source transformers; S&P A- boost, emissions down 8%. Zeta $0.28 EPS hit but NPS 78, core 4.2% ROE.

On investments in renewables and clean transition, we deployed $2.4 billion capex 45% of total, up from 32%, adding 1.2 GW solar in ERCOT/SPP, 650 MW Midwest PJM wind, 450 MWh BESS like 200 MW/800 MWh Ironwood at 92% efficiency, 12% IRR ancillaries. Renewables 38% capacity from 28%, 42% MWh clean excluding nuclear, $850 million EBITDA up 15% despite soft prices; 95% PPAs at $45/MWh solar, $38 wind above $30 LCOE on 40% module drop. Bifacial TOPCon with Nextracker at 28-30% factors; Vestas/GE high-hub wind +25% repower; 70% hybrids like 500 MW/2 GWh Desert Peak for duck curve/RA. IRA ITC 55% yields on $1.1 billion solar, PTC 45Y for 800 MW wind; ERCOT 2.5 GW queue with FTRs/gas firming; PJM RPM stacking post-Order 2222. UK/Ireland 400 MW offshore with Orsted at £50/MWh CfD hedging ETS €100/tonne; 50 MW green H2 at coal site 20% cheaper. Divested 1.2 GW coal at 8x EBITDA to $5 billion JV with BlackRock/Brookfield; 10-12% IRR, breakeven $60/tonne CO2; 85% contracted supply. $3.2 billion 2024 capex 55% renewables for 2 GW/1 GWh, 65% renewable capacity by 2030, $2.5 billion clean EBITDA.

Reliability metrics show weather-normalized Q3 SAIDI at 78.4 minutes, down 12% YoY from 89.2, SAIFI 0.92 from 1.08; full-year SAIDI 112.6 from 128.4, 12.3% better, SAIFI 1.18 from 1.42, 17% gain—top-quartile vs EEI medians, like Duke/PSE. Third year double-digit gains on $450 million program; non-normalized higher at 145/1.45 on 18 MED days vs 9, from Idaho winds/Midwest ice, CAIDI steady 95. PNW 92 minutes on 1.2 million spans trim/LiDAR drones, zero PSPS; Midwest 1.32 SAIFI on ADMS cutting detection 40%; Northeast/Southwest 105/118, covered conductors under 1.1 SAIFI. 98% AMI 3.8 million Itron meters flagging 65% faults; Overstory AI trim to 3 years; 50 MW Fluence grid-forming inverters. $1.2 billion 2024 capex 25% reliability: 500 miles undergrounding, NERC CIP-014. De-risks rates/ROE to 10.2%, DER aggregation; 5-7% improvement guide.

Rate base grew from $28.4 billion year-start to $29.7 billion, 4.6% or $1.3 billion adds, on track 5.2-5.5% to 6% five-year CAGR. $1.8 billion regulated capex up 12%, 55% T&D, 30% gen renewables/storage, AFUDC $120 million at 4.8% costs post $500 million green bonds. Gen: 450 MW SolarPeak +200 MW BESS $650 million CWIP, 15% factors capturing RPS/Order 2222; 800 MW wind-storage $1.2 billion. T&D: $450 million Cardinal-Harding 345 kV for data centers on 2.8% MISO load growth, 15 GW data/EV 1.2 GW. Dist: $550 million AMI/DERMS, Tennessee $200 million rider. Headwinds: dep 8% to $950 million on coal idles; 9-11% inflation squeezing 20 bps ARO, 70% fixed EPC; delays mitigated. Formula rates 85% auto-flow; Indiana case $300 million 60% CWIP 7.5% ROE. 8-10% hurdles, $250 million IRA credits; $34.5 billion by 2027 for 6-7% EPS.

Finally, fossil retirements and replacements. Decommissioned 1.2 GW subcritical coal past 24 months, including 650 MW Willow Creek MISO at 35% factor/11,000 heat rate, $85 million costs from $200 million reserve; 800 MW Black Mesa ERCOT by Q4 2025 ahead SB7, $120 million annual savings. Plan 2.1 GW more: 1.5 GW coal/600 MW peakers, emissions to 400 lbs/MWh by 2030 ahead peers. $450 million impairment offset $300 million 45Q/$150 million queues. Replacements: 900 MW post-Willow—500 MW First Solar bifacial DC/AC 28.5 +250 MWh Tesla 60% factor PPA Amazon 32/MWh $750 million 7.5% IRR 30% ITC+bonus; Black Mesa 700 MW Orsted GE wind 55% +300 MWh Form iron-air $1.8 billion DOE loans. CAISO: 400 MW H2-ready NGCC GE H-class 45/MWh 45V; MISO nuclear $300 million uprates. Repurposing cuts NEPA 18 months; Fluence AI 15% ancillaries; 50 MW blue H2 95% capture 45Q $85/ton. Hedged natgas $2.80, 10% additionality; 70% locked panels. Unlocks $1.2 billion FCF by 2030, 11% ROIC 6-8% EBITDA CAGR.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Maria Gonzalez to discuss the financials.

Maria Gonzalez: Thank you, Johnathan. Good morning, everyone. For the Q3, we reported earnings per share of $0.85 and revenue of $2.45 billion. Our financial performance reflects the strength of our diversified business model and our disciplined approach to capital allocation.

Our capital expenditure for the quarter was $650 million, primarily focused on renewable integrations and grid hardening. We remain committed to maintaining a strong balance sheet and returning value to shareholders. We anticipate EPS growth of 6-8% in 2025.

David Chen: Thank you, Maria. Let me provide an update on the operational front. We are seeing improved efficiency in our natural gas combined-cycle power plants due to the implementation of AI predictive maintenance. This has resulted in an 18% increase in output. Our outage rates are also down 25%.

Lisa Patel: Thank you, David. Turning to our long-term strategy, we are actively exploring opportunities in the battery storage space. We believe this will be a key driver of future growth. We are also evaluating potential acquisitions in the Midwest market.

Robert Kim: Thank you, Lisa. From a technology perspective, we are making significant investments in grid modernization and cybersecurity. We recently deployed quantum-secure encryption platform to enhance our defenses against cyber threats. We are also piloting advanced synchrophasors in ERCOT market.

Emily Torres: Thank you, Robert. On the regulatory front, we received approval for our rate case settlement in Texas. This will allow us to recover $300 million in infrastructure costs.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you, Maria, David, Lisa, Robert, and Emily. Now, we'll open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Sarah Jenkins with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins: Good morning. Can you elaborate on your plans for renewable expansion?

Johnathan Hale: Certainly. As I detailed earlier, we're leading with $3.2 billion in 2024 capex targeting 2 GW additions and 1 GWh storage, scaling to 65% renewables by 2030 through hybrids, IRA incentives, and PPAs, all while hitting 12-14% returns.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mike Larson with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Mike Larson: What is your outlook for customer usage trends?

Maria Gonzalez: Our diversified profile supports 2.8-3.2% load growth FY24, driven by EVs, data centers, and industrial reshoring, offset by efficiency but tailwinds dominate for sustained EPS.

Operator: Our next question comes from David Ruiz with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

David Ruiz: How are you mitigating risks related to storm impacts?

David Chen: Through $2.5 billion resiliency including AI weather, hardening, and mutual aid, we've cut SAIDI 15% event-over-event and positioned for lower future costs with insurance recoveries.

Operator: Our next question comes from Sarah Jenkins with Greenleaf Capital. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins: What is the anticipated impact of fossil retirements on your earnings?

Emily Torres: Retirements unlock $1.2 billion FCF by 2030 at 11% ROIC via low-LCOE replacements with tax credits and PPAs, minimally dilutive short-term but accretive long-term to 6-8% EBITDA growth.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the call back over to Johnathan Hale for closing remarks.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you. In summary, we delivered solid results in the Q3, demonstrating the strength of our business model and our commitment to creating long-term value for our shareholders. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and positioning GridPower Holdings for continued success. Thank you for your time and interest in GridPower Holdings.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
